statements.proposition: This change is fully backward compatible while fixing the Python 3.14 event-loop crash.
statements.label: CANNOT_TELL
statements.note: Impact claim with no settling check. Structurally, the only library change wraps asyncio.get_event_loop() in try/except RuntimeError and creates a new loop on failure, so the path where get_event_loop() succeeds is the same as before. That supports the claim but does not settle it: on older Pythons a call that used to raise RuntimeError (for example from a non-main thread with no loop) now creates a loop instead, and whether that counts as a compatibility break is a judgment call. No public name or signature changed. Also: the PR text says get_running_loop() is tried first, but the code at head calls get_event_loop(); this does not affect this proposition.
